## Acceptance criteria

<!-- What must be true for this feature to ship. One bullet each, in the form
     `- **AC1.** <behavior>`, and each one testable as written — a reader should be able to tell
     whether it holds without asking you.

     Number them in order and never reuse a number. If you delete a criterion, leave the gap:
     tests elsewhere cite these numbers, and reusing one silently repoints a test at different
     behavior. See [[_authoring:wiki-page-ids#row-and-criterion-ids]].

     Which criteria belong here: the ones spanning several of this feature's flows, or stating a
     commitment about the capability as a whole. Criteria about one flow's steps live on that flow
     instead — the product README draws the line. If every criterion has moved to a flow, point at
     the flows under Task flows rather than writing "None.".

     Naming things: link entities as [[domain:entities/<name>]] (or `[[product:entities/<module>/<name>]]` for a persisted twin). Where a criterion turns on a
     stored value, name the field as inline `code`, matching the entity's `## Data model`; where it
     describes what the user sees, use the label they see. Summary and User story stay in plain user
     language throughout. Where a criterion depends on who the user is, link the access-model
     ([[product:concepts/access-model]] if authored; otherwise name the role in prose). Where it
     restates a rule that applies across the product, link the governing policy
     ([[product:concepts/policies/<slug>]]) instead of repeating it. -->

- **AC1.** <observable behavior that must be true for the feature to ship>

## Quality attributes

<!-- How well this capability must work, as opposed to what it must do — speed, availability,
     security, accessibility. One bullet each, testable as written. These are often called
     non-functional requirements (NFRs). Requirements that belong to the whole module or the whole
     system go elsewhere; the product README draws that line. -->

## Task flows

<!-- The task flows this feature delivers — one bullet per flow, usually the flows this feature
     owns. A hub feature that owns no flow of its own lists the flows it frames and says so in the
     section's first line.

     List every flow whose tests prove one of the criteria above. A criterion counts as covered only
     when a flow named here proves it, so a flow you leave out makes its criteria read as untested.

     List the module-specific flow first, then any shared base flow it builds on:
       `[[flows/<module>/<task>]] — <what the user accomplishes>`
       `[[flows/_shared/<task>]] — <what the user accomplishes>`
     Each bullet opens with its flow link, then ` — ` and the outcome; the audit errors on a bullet that
     does not and on a link to a page that is not a `task-flow`. A hub feature's lead line before the
     first bullet is not graded.
     Plain language — no entity field names. Flow sharing/specialization and hub-feature rules: see `task-flow`. -->

     a modal or a step in a wizard. One bullet each, in plain product language. This is the list of

     Name each surface's kind, one of the surface kinds the wiki engine ships (listed, a one-line

       - **<Surface name>** (<kind>) — <one line>. States: <applicable app-ux-resilience states>. -->
